items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: The interviewee discusses Joe Williams' relationship with Basie ('relationship was excellent with Basie') and mentions Basie in the context of Williams' career, but does not describe a direct personal or professional interaction between himself (John Levy) and Count Basie.

ctx.x: And like what was the status—

That was the time when Basie finally broke up and had the six pieces, you know, because it was really rough out there for big bands. But groups like George was really hot, and Dave Brubeck, and that was the hottest things going, playing the colleges and you know, so it was really — the big band it just cost too much to travel. And the economics of it at that time was even worse than they are now. I mean they’re bad enough now, but for a big band it was terrible, you know. But anyway, that’s how I got into that…

business. And then one by one different people came along. And I knew Joe, for years I’d known Joe Williams. And when he left the Basie band and he called me one day he said, “come and take this telephone out of my hands.”

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Another room especially that Basie worked in... That’s where Shirley Scott and – even Basie played organ in there

ctx.x: Another room especially that Basie worked in, and a room that was an organ group – it was a room that played mostly organs. That’s where Shirley Scott and – even Basie played organ in there – this particular club – with a small group, before the big-band – all his big-band experience, which came later on. The uptown, or Harlem, clubs catered to more of especially creative things. In other words, they did more shows where they would have a comedian and a singer and then a tap-dancer or something. It was more like…
I want to jump back to Chicago a little bit, because we – the Garrick Stage Bar. That’s where you had hooked up with Stuff.
